business_scope.primary_industry_name: Internet Retailing of Outdoor Sports and Camping Gear

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Samoa (International Companies regime under the International Companies Act 1987)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English common law statutory foundation with indigenous customary law elements and local statutory framework)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: PACER Plus (Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus) — Services and Investment chapter
Samoa–People's Republic of China Belt and Road Economic Cooperation Framework (investment facilitation)
Tax Information Exchange Agreements (TIEAs) with Australia, New Zealand and the United States

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended), s.XX (register of members); Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (as amended); Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2007; Samoa International Finance Authority Act 1996; Companies Act 2001; FATF Recommendation 24 (beneficial ownership) as implemented through SIFA AML/CFT Guidance Notes

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association (Constitutional Documents)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) registered agent / notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via Samoa Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (MFAT) — Samoa is a Contracting Party; China acceptance effective 7 November 2023

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (extract from SIFA Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via MFAT (for PRC banks and counterparties)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Existence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, for non-Convention states, consular legalization through the Samoa Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade and the destination embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO Declaration and Registered Officer Consent (Piercing disclosure for AML file)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal AML file — not notarized externally; notarized only when required by the PRC regulator

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against the Samoa FIU watchlist, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, OFAC SDN list, UK HMT and PRC MFA sanctions list; PEP status determination via risk-ranked questionnaires and private-source database checks; enhanced due diligence (EDD) applies to PEPs, source-of-wealth verification, and sanctions hits (MLPA 2007, Parts IV–V); results preserved in the AML file for five years from relationship termination.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) e-Services Company Registry (https://www.sifa.ws) — International Companies Name Reservation and Registration module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Primary name must be in Latin script (English); a transliterated or vernacular second name (e.g., Chinese 中文 name) is permitted as an additional registered name provided the Latin-character primary name is distinct and fileable; all diacritics are normalized to ASCII; the name must end with a required designation such as 'Limited', 'Ltd.', or 'Corporation'.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banker, Banking, Banana Bank, or any term implying banking business (requires Central Bank / FIU license and approval)
Trust, Trustee, or Trust Company (requires trustee license under SIFA regulation)
Insurance, Assurance, Reinsurance, Insurer (requires insurance regulatory license)
Finance, Financial, Credit, Securities, Fund, Investment (requires financial services authorization)
Government, Ministry, National, Crown, Authority, Samoa Pacific or any token suggesting state patronage or intergovernmental status (requires Cabinet/Registrar consent)
International (requires SIFA characterization as International Company)
The Commonwealth, United Nations, or international organization names (prohibited)
Offshore, Tax Haven, or similar terms (rejected on public interest grounds)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Where the Registrar of International Companies rejects a name, the applicant must receive a written statement of grounds; an administrative appeal must be filed at the SIFA registry within 14 calendar days of rejection, supported by a memorandum of legal argument and, if applicable, the ministerial or regulatory consent letter (e.g., Central Bank approval for banking tokens); the appeal will be determined by the Registrar with reference to the international company name guidelines within 10 business days; if the refusal is reaffirmed, a fresh application may be made under a revised name or a judicial review petition to the Supreme Court of Samoa may be filed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted as sole registered office — every International Company must maintain a registered office in Samoa at the licensed registered agent's physical address; the office must be accessible during business hours, receive legal process, and hold the statutory registers; a non-resident e-commerce operator may conduct all trading outside Samoa (no physical presence required) as long as the SIFA-licensed registered agent service is retained.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate — estimated 10% within the first year for a low-risk e-commerce international company; SIFA and the Samoa FIU hold statutory inspection and document-production powers and may conduct on-site verification of the registered agent's premises and records without prior notice, particularly in jurisdictions flagged by APG peer review.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.primary_regulator_note: SIFA exercises day-to-day supervision of International Companies; the Registrar may demand production of books and records within a specified period.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), ss. 6, 8, 14, 33, 50 and Schedule 1 (Fees); read with the Companies Act 2001 for general procedural matters not inconsistent with the IC Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Companies and Trusts Office (SICTO), Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association (Form 1 – Application for Incorporation of an International Company)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an International Company; at least one issued share with or without par value is required. No escrow account deposit is imposed for standard international company incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscribers of the Samoa International Company adopt this First Board Resolution. 1. Share Subscription: That the initial issued shares be allotted to the first-named subscriber in accordance with the incorporation application, and that the share register be opened immediately. 2. Registered Office: That the registered office be situated at Level 2, Samoa International Companies and Trusts Office, Apia, Samoa, and that the licensed registered agent be retained for service of process. 3. Officers: That the persons nominated in the incorporation application be appointed as Director and Secretary, each with authority to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and administer the Company's online retail operations. Approved and effective as of the date inserted below.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and International Company Agent Appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Companies and Trusts Office (SICTO), Registration Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed international company agent in Samoa. Submit a name reservation request to SICTO either by physical lodgment or through the agent's electronic filing portal, confirming the proposed name is not identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered company or reserved name. Upon approval, the name is reserved for 30 days.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation of agent (if applicable)
Passport copy and proof of address of beneficial owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit a new name reservation within 5 business days or file an administrative appeal with SICTO explaining distinctiveness within 15 days of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed International Company Agent / Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The licensed agent prepares the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English, containing the company name, proposed share capital, broad objects clause, registered office clause, and the powers of directors. The documents are executed by the subscriber as a deed before a notary public.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association draft
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SICTO returns the governing documents for correction, amend the relevant clauses and re-execute the documents; resubmission within 10 business days avoids a fresh filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application and Statutory Declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge Form 1 (Application for Incorporation) with the executed Memorandum and Articles, the registered agent's consent, the registered office consent, and declarations of the initial directors and secretary. Verify that the appointment of directors and secretary complies with the International Companies Act 1987.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Statement of preservation of records by registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition for further particulars, the licensed agent must file a compliant response and pay any query fee within 14 days of service; failure to respond results in deemed withdrawal, requiring a fresh application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Statutory Fees and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pay the SICTO filing fee, company registration fee, and any applicable urgent processing fee by wire transfer or registered agent's trust account. Upon validation of payment, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation with a unique company number and date of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Payment receipt or bank transfer confirmation
Funded client account statement of the licensed agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If payment is not credited, provide proof of wire remittance and request SICTO to trace the funds; if the certificate is withheld due to pending GST or government fees, settle the outstanding amount within 48 hours to release the certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution and Appointment of Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors, Samoa International Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Certificate of Incorporation is issued, the sole subscriber or initial directors pass the written First Board Resolution in accordance with the articles. The resolution records share allotment, adoption of the registered office, and the appointment of the director and secretary. All consents are signed and filed in the company's statutory register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an officer appointment is void due to lack of consent, convene a written shareholders' resolution to ratify the choice or appoint a substitute, and re-file the consent forms with SICTO within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Exemption Confirmation and Post-Incorporation Compliance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa Ministry of Revenue and SICTO Compliance Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a Certificate of Tax Exemption confirming the International Company is exempt from income tax, stamp duty, and exchange control under the International Companies Act 1987. No goods and services tax registration is required for offshore e-commerce transactions. Maintain the registered agent and register of charges.
required_dossiers: Registered agent confirmation of ongoing registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax exemption certificate is refused due to a deviation from offshore scope, submit a standard representation letter confirming that all sales of outdoor camping equipment are concluded outside Samoa or are export transactions; a revised application is processed within 7 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – the enterprise conducts internet retailing of outdoor sports and camping gear; no manufacturing, processing, or physical industrial operation is undertaken in Samoa.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required – no operational or manufacturing permit applies to a pure e-commerce retail International Company under Samoa law.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Division of Environment and Conservation, Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no fixed industrial installation or land-disturbing activity; an EIA registration is not triggered by virtual retail warehousing of packaged consumer goods.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the core activity. If a local warehouse is used, stormwater runoff must remain clean and uncontaminated; any waste packaging must be segregated and recycled under the Waste Management Act 2005, and no VOC or hazardous chemical emissions are permitted from storage of sealed camping equipment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire safety or structural certification is required for a purely virtual office. If a physical warehouse or storage depot is established in Samoa, the operator must obtain a Fire Safety Certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority, verify floor-loading limits under the Samoa National Building Code, and obtain a workplace clearance confirming safe shelving, egress, and fire suppression equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Ministry of Revenue (MOR) – online portal: Samoa Tax Portal (SatisTax, https://revenue.gov.ws)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: An International Company (IC) formed under the Samoa International Companies Act 1987 is not automatically registered for Samoan income tax. If the IC carries on a taxable activity in Samoa or derives Samoa-source income, it must apply to the Ministry of Revenue for a TIN using Form IRD-TIN-01 and register for direct taxes. Purely offshore ICs with no Samoa-source income and no local activity may obtain a tax exemption certificate from MOR without TIN registration. VAGST registration, where applicable, is made separately on Form VAGST-REG-01.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa does not operate a check-the-box pass-through election. An IC may, however, voluntarily register for VAGST if it conducts taxable activities, and may apply to MOR for a tax exemption certificate confirming its offshore income exemption. Hybrid mismatch elections are not recognised in Samoa's tax legislation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory e-invoicing or real-time fiscal clearance system is in force. Tax invoices must meet VAGST requirements (supplier name, TIN, date, description, GST amount) but no government API clearance or digital stamping is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from Samoa are chargeable to VAGST at 0% where the goods are physically exported out of Samoa within the prescribed period and evidence of export is retained. Offshore services supplied to a non-resident outside Samoa qualify for 0% if the services are not performed for the benefit of a person in Samoa and the supplier satisfies MOR documentary requirements.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Inward Remittance Certificate (bank evidence of foreign exchange receipt)
Certificate of Origin (where preferential tariff treatment is claimed)
Supplier's formal declaration of export status under VAGST rules
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or unsupported zero-rating claims attract immediate VAGST assessment at the standard 15% rate, together with late payment penalty of 20% per annum, a 20% shortfall penalty, and potential criminal liability under the Goods and Services Tax Act for deliberately evading tax or presenting false documentation. Retrospective clawback extends to all input credits wrongly claimed in connection with the non-qualifying export.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), acting as the Exchange Control Authority pursuant to the Exchange Control Act 1976 and the Exchange Control Regulations 1976 (as amended)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan tālā (WST) operates under a system of partial convertibility. Current account transactions are generally liberalized, subject to documentation and exchange control declaration. Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment equity subscriptions in an international company, are subject to prior CBS approval and submission of Form BOP/FDI. Profit remittance is lawful but subject to withholding tax on dividends, production of audited financial statements, tax clearance certificate, and exchange control approval demonstrating that the underlying investment was properly admitted.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: All export receipts from a Samoa-domiciled international company must be repatriated to Samoa within ninety (90) days of export and surrendered to a licensed commercial bank. The mandatory conversion requirement is 100% of foreign currency export proceeds converted into WST or retained in a designated foreign currency account only with prior CBS approval. Proceeds may be retained offshore only under a standing exemption granted to shipping or certain service-export entities; for ISIC 4791 e-commerce retail, no general exemption applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (in WST and foreign currency)
Capital Escrow Account (for inward capital injection and profit escrow)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability. Samoa does not maintain a fintech EMI or electronic money institution licensing regime. Offshore digital EMI account providers cannot legally establish banking facilities for Samoa-domiciled international companies without obtaining a commercial bank licence under the Financial Institutions Act 1996. Payment aggregation via Stripe/PayPal is acceptable as a settlement conduit but cannot replace licensed banking relationships. International companies should therefore rely on tier-1 domestic banks with correspondent banking networks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: CBS AML/CFT rules generally require face-to-face verification for new bank relationships. However, for an international company licensed under the International Companies Act 1987, banks commonly accept remote onboarding via a licensed trustee, registered agent, or introducing broker using certified passport copies, notarized proof of address, corporate due diligence packages, and video KYC interviews. In practice, at least one beneficial owner or a director with signing authority must appear electronically for an interview; full physical presence in Samoa can be waived for low-risk retail technology businesses provided source of funds and commercial purpose are fully documented.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: International Company (IC) with no local economic substance or physical office
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered agent certificate of incumbency, current Certificate of Good Standing, annual return filing confirmation, detailed board resolution describing online retail operations, Shopify/Stripe/PayPal settlement reports, and an ancillary service agreement with the Samoa registered agent documenting controlled asset management.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner resident in a jurisdiction on the FATF monitoring list or with opaque company registers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Individual passport and national ID, utility bill not older than three months, professional background and source-of-wealth statement, bank reference letter from the beneficial owner's principal bank, and an organizational chart proving the ownership chain to each ultimate beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected transactional flows from card settlement aggregators with high velocity and cross-border e-commerce counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed terms of service from Stripe/PayPal, platform transaction summary for the past twelve months, export invoices and outbound shipping carrier airway bills, customs export declarations under HS 9403 (furniture) or HS 6306 (canvas goods), and the company's anti-fraud and refund policy for outdoor camping gear.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Advance payments or capital injections from related non-resident entities where economic rationale is not self-evident
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Intercompany loan or capital subscription agreement, board minutes approving the injection, bank statement showing counterparty debits, investor asset verification, and CBS Form BOP/FDI application with supporting feasibility study.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Named beneficiary or counterparty in UBO registry is politically exposed or high-net-worth with unexplained wealth
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Specialized AML enhanced due diligence report from a licensed investigative agency, sworn declaration of income, tax returns from the country of residence, and a licensed trust or family office structure chart showing independent trustee governance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital for the Samoa IC is routed via SWIFT MT103 from the ultimate beneficial owner's bank using purpose code under the IMF BPM6: 'FDI-equity injection' or 'Other Investment-Loan to related enterprise'. The transfer must name the exact IC legal name, registration number, and Samoa domestic bank account IBAN or CBC-number. A copy of the CBS pre-registration approval or Form BOP/FDI acceptance must accompany the transfer. Where the capital is deployed for raw inventory of camping equipment, the remitter should additionally reference 'ISIC 4791 online retail working capital'. The domestic beneficiary bank will require the source-of-funds certificate and a board resolution before crediting a Capital Escrow Account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements may be cleared through SWIFT MT103 for suppliers under USD 250,000 equivalent; for larger manufacturing purchase orders, a confirmed irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit issued by the Samoan bank is the preferred rail. Payments to overseas outdoor gear manufacturers are made via correspondent bank clearance through ANZ or common Pacific correspondent networks. Settlement currencies permitted are WST, USD, AUD, NZD, and EUR at CBS-approved exchange rates. Each outward remittance must reference the underlying commercial invoice, shipping terms, and customs tariff code, and must be supported by exchange control form 'PCA-01' for trade payments when exceeding CBS thresholds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CBS-licensed commercial bank forward contracts for INCLUSIVE of export proceeds and trade import payables, maturing up to 360 days, requiring valid trade documentation
Currency swaps between WST and USD/Basket of major currencies executed through an authorized Samoan dealer with prior CBS notification for hedging only, not speculation
CBS-approved currency options for offshore project finance-related cashflows; not generally available for standard retail e-commerce, and only with demonstrated underlying trade exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form AR-IC) of International Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA), Companies Office / Registrar of International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due not later than six (6) calendar months after the anniversary of the date of incorporation of the International Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 20% of the annual fee for the first 60 days of non-compliance, an additional 20% penalty for the next 60 days, and administrative strike-off from the Samoa International Companies Register if filings remain outstanding beyond 120 days after the due date

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Confirmation Statement of Registered Details (including registered office, directors, and shareholders record)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA), Registry of International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the anniversary of incorporation; a filing on change of details is required within 21 days of any relevant change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Daily default penalty imposed for late filing of changes; repeated default may result in request for removal of the International Company from the Register

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory independent audit is required for ordinary International Companies with fewer than 10 shareholders and total assets below USD 500,000; a certified audit becomes compulsory if shareholders representing at least 10% of the issued shares request it, or if the International Company is classified as a public interest entity under Samoa regulations
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa) and International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted by Samoa for entities requiring statutory accounts; smaller International Companies may apply practical accounting standards under local GAAP exemptions

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every International Company must maintain a Register of Beneficial Owners at its registered office and submit an annual beneficial ownership confirmation to the Samoa Registry before the anniversary date; any transfer of shares during the year must be updated in the UBO register no later than 14 days after the effective transfer, with a written notification filed with the Registrar within 14 days thereafter

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 – USD 1,200 per annum for licensed registered agent and registered office services for a standard International Company
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 – USD 3,500 per annum for a certified public accountant audit of a low-risk, e-commerce retailing International Company

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% for resident domestic companies under the Income Tax Act 1974 (as amended), subject to temporary and sectoral variations.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Companies Act 1988 (Part XIII, s.115): International Companies (IC) transacting business entirely outside Samoa are exempt from Samoan income tax and stamp duty; the effective rate is therefore 0%. No statutory tax holiday is offered; the exemption is a blanket statutory exclusion for ICs that do not derive Samoa-source income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No IR-1 corporate income tax return is required for an exempt International Company. The operative filing is the Annual Declaration / Certificate of Compliance submitted to the Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA) through a licensed registered agent on the SIFA digital registry portal. Domestic resident companies file Form IR-1 with the Ministry for Revenue via the Samoa Tax Online e-filing system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: IC: within 30 days before the anniversary of incorporation each year. Domestic IR-1: within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year (standard fiscal year end 30 September; a 31 December year end is permissible on Ministerial approval).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name and SIFA registration number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the full name as registered under the International Companies Act 1988; no Samoan tax identification number is required for an exempt IC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered agent and registered office address in Samoa
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory engagement of a SIFA-licensed registered agent; a P.O. Box address is acceptable; a physical Samoa office is not required.
Nominee directors and corporate shareholders are permissible; non-resident individuals and entities may hold 100% ownership.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Issued share capital and beneficial ownership declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No minimum capital applies; ultimate beneficial owners must be disclosed to the registered agent for the SIFA beneficial ownership register.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certification that no business is carried on within Samoa
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The certifying officer must confirm zero Samoa-source revenue, zero local payroll, and zero Samoan shipping or e-commerce sales to preserve the 0% tax exemption.

Provide a concise narrative confirming board oversight through the registered agent, adequate records of the internet retail operations, and that core income-generating activities are directed from Samoa.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing incurs a surcharge of WST 200 per month or part thereof, capped at WST 1,000, plus a reinstatement penalty of up to WST 500 if the company is struck off. Persistent non-filing leads to compulsory strike-off, loss of limited liability protection, and disqualification of the registered agent where culpable.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory non-resident dividend withholding tax under the Income Tax Act 1974 where dividends are paid out of Samoa-source profits. For an exempt International Company, dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders are outside the Samoan tax net and suffer 0% Samoan withholding tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Samoa's DTA network is limited (notably New Zealand, Australia, Norway, Austria, and a limited arrangement with China). The protocol requires: (a) obtain a Certificate of Residence from the Samoa Ministry for Revenue; (b) submit the source-state's reduced-withholding form together with the Samoan tax return when claiming treaty benefits; and (c) for ICs, instead claim the statutory exemption via a SIFA Certificate of Exemption countersigned by the registered agent. No advance rating is required before distribution, and the exemption applies from the date the IC certifies it has not carried on business in Samoa.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates for Samoa-source payments: interest 15% and royalties 15%. Treaty rates may reduce interest and royalties where the counterparty resides in a treaty jurisdiction. ICs collecting e-commerce card royalties, payment processing interest, or platform fees from Stripe/PayPal outside Samoa are exempt from Samoan WHT at 0%, provided the income source is not Samoa.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Samoa applies transfer pricing rules under the Income Tax Act 1974 (s.34C as amended) only to resident taxpayers with cross-border connected person transactions; no statutory local-currency monetary threshold is promulgated. Exempt ICs are not within the transfer pricing net while the 0% exemption subsists. As a benchmarking proxy, practitioners commonly retain Master File/Local File documentation when consolidated turnover exceeds WST 5,000,000, although this amount is not a legal trigger.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The International Companies (Economic Substance) Regulations 2021 apply to ICs engaged in defined relevant activities, expressly including distribution and service centre business, which captures the internet retailing of outdoor camping equipment. The IC must demonstrate: board management and decision-taking performed in Samoa through the registered agent; adequate staff, premises, and annual operating expenditure; and core income-generating activities directed and controlled from Samoa. Passive reselling without local substance or booking arrangements in third countries triggers a gap in the exemption and exposes the IC to challenge before the SIFA Economic Substance Committee.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deriving Samoa-source revenue (e.g., sales to Samoan consumers, local delivery fees, or Shopify store servicing Samoan customers) while falsely certifying Item 5 of the SIFA declaration that no business is conducted in Samoa, thereby unlawfully preserving the 0% rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-assessment of all undeclared profits at the 27% corporate rate, plus a civil penalty equal to 100% of the tax shortfall and interest at 6% per annum under the Income Tax Act 1974. Criminal fines of up to WST 1,000,000 apply on indictment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who sign or knowingly permit a false certification are personally liable on a joint and several basis for the back taxes and penalties. Under the Crimes Act 2013, knowing provision of false information to a public authority attracts imprisonment of up to 7 years and disqualification of the director from acting as an IC director for 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the IC as a zero-substance e-commerce reseller with no office, no agent involvement, no books, and no economic activity outside Samoa, while using the SIFA attestation to portray a genuine offshore trading business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Strike-off under the International Companies Act 1988 without restoration; revocation of the registered agent's licence where the agent aided the sham; mandatory referral to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit and disclosure on the beneficial ownership register; permanent ineligibility for a future IC licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal liability for all SIFA fees, restitution to third-party creditors, and a travel ban under the Frauds Act. Criminal conviction for furnishing false information to the Registrar carries imprisonment of up to 7 years and automatic disqualification from corporate management in Samoa.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the IC as a pass-through payment vehicle for undisclosed merchants using Stripe/PayPal, failing to maintain beneficial ownership records, or layering online retail proceeds through nominee bank accounts to obscure the ultimate recipient.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 and SIFA AML/CFT Rules, pecuniary penalties of up to WST 100,000 per breach, suspension or revocation of the registered agent's licence, and a directive to freeze the IC's bank accounts. The risk tier elevated to high risk where the low-risk standard category of ISIC 4791 is abused.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible officers are individually liable for imprisonment of up to 14 years and fines of up to WST 1,000,000 where money laundering is proved. Directors may be barred from holding any position in a financial institution or licensed agent for 10 years, and the court may order civil asset forfeiture of the total funds laundered.
